questions.prompt: Scores of 7 students in each of two classes: class P: 70, 74, 76, 78, 80, 82, 86; class Q: 66, 70, 72, 74, 76, 78, 82. Which comparison of centers is appropriate and correct?
questions.prompt_markup: Scores of 7 students in each of two classes: class P: 70, 74, 76, 78, 80, 82, 86; class Q: 66, 70, 72, 74, 76, 78, 82. Which comparison of centers is appropriate and correct?

choices.text: Compare medians: P's median 76 is 2 points above Q's median 74, so P is 2 points higher.
Compare the highest scores: P's 86 is 4 points above Q's 82, so P is 4 points higher.
Both are roughly symmetric with no outliers, so compare means: P's mean 78 is 4 points above Q's mean 74.
Both are roughly symmetric, so compare means: P's mean 76 is 2 points above Q's mean 74.

questions.correct_answer: Both are roughly symmetric with no outliers, so compare means: P's mean 78 is 4 points above Q's mean 74.
questions.grading_note: Means: 546/7 = 78 and 518/7 = 74 (the medians are also 78 and 74). The others miscompute the mean or median of P, or compare maximums, which do not describe the center.

questions.prompt: Heights (cm) of 7 seedlings of each of two plants: plant A: 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 8, 30; plant B: 8, 8, 9, 9, 9, 10, 10. Which comparison of typical heights is appropriate?
questions.prompt_markup: Heights (cm) of 7 seedlings of each of two plants: plant A: 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 8, 30; plant B: 8, 8, 9, 9, 9, 10, 10. Which comparison of typical heights is appropriate?

choices.text: Compare means: A's mean (about 9.9 cm) is greater, so A's seedlings are typically taller.
Compare means: both are about 9 cm, so the seedlings are typically the same height.
Compare maximums: A's tallest seedling (30 cm) is taller, so A's seedlings are typically taller.

questions.grading_note: A's mean 69/7 ≈ 9.86 is pulled up by 30; medians 7 and 9 describe typical seedlings. The others use the mean despite the outlier or use the maximum.
